name: maybe_Ui_IconCache_BeginLoad

name: maybe_Ui_IconCache_FinishLoad

name: maybe_Ui_IconCache_LoadForPanel

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieTrack_Create
signature: u32 maybe_Gfx_MovieTrack_Create(u32 channel, u32 streamId, u32 frameCount)

params.frameCount: number of 0x18-byte frame entries to allocate

Returns the slot index, 0 on allocation failure and 0xFFFFFFFF when no slot is free.

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieTrack_Pause
summary: Pauses a movie track by sending decoder state 2 to its handle, under the player lock. Out-of-range indices are ignored.
evidence: Same guard (arg < count at 0x007AE168) and same lock/sleep dance as the neighbouring track functions; the payload is 0x0051A4AC(handle, 2), and 0x0051A4AC sets the decoder state byte and calls the channel stop helper 0x00518D04.

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieTrack_Resume
summary: Resumes a paused movie track by sending decoder state 0 to its handle, under the player lock.
evidence: Identical to 0x004FC4CC except for the state argument (0 instead of 2) passed to 0x0051A4AC; both are unlocked public helpers over the 0x007AE154 track table.

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieTrack_QueueBuffer
signature: u32 maybe_Gfx_MovieTrack_QueueBuffer(u32 track, void* data, u32 size)

params.data: buffer to hand to the decoder

summary: Queues one input buffer for a movie track: it refuses when the track has no pending frame or when the 64-entry completion ring is full, flushes the buffer for DMA with 0x001122D0 and pushes {track,data,size} into the ring at 0x007C805C. Returns 1 when queued and 0 otherwise.
evidence: The ring is 0x40 * 0x0C entries indexed by '+0x18 & 0x3F' and drained by 0x004FC8A8; '+0x50' counts outstanding buffers and '+0x38' is the expected frame count written by 0x004FC230; the 'already busy' condition (f_18 - f_1C == 0x40) matches a fixed 64-entry queue.

name: maybe_Gfx_Movie_WaitForTracks
summary: Flushes the movie player until every track reports idle: it sets the 'draining' byte, calls the update pump 0x004FC8A8 while no track has work left and sleeps 5,000,000 ticks (0x004C4B40) between polls. This is vtable slot 2 of the movie player (base 0x00780C14).
evidence: Sits in vtable 0x00780C14 = [0x004FC7FC, 0x004FC7EC, 0x004FC794] (slot 2); the sleep constant 0x004C4B40 = 5,000,000 is the same 5-second poll used by 0x004FE6F4/0x004FE94C; the loop condition is the manager byte at 0x007AE155.

name: maybe_Gfx_MoviePlayer_AddRef

params.self: movie context; the reference counter is global at 0x007AE164

summary: Adds one reference to the global movie-context counter and, on the first reference, initialises the mixer/buffer object embedded at +0xAB0. Used by the window code before starting playback.
evidence: Increments the same global word (+0x10 of 0x007AE154) that 0x004FC85C decrements; it calls 0x004FE0A4 on self+0xC88 and 0x004FE88C on self+0xAB0 only while the 'initialised' byte at +0x1051 is clear, mirroring the teardown in 0x004FC85C.

name: maybe_Gfx_MoviePlayer_ReleaseRef
summary: Drops one reference to the movie context and, when it was initialised, shuts the embedded buffer object down. Exact counterpart of 0x004FC808.
evidence: Decrements the 0x007AE154 reference count and calls 0x004FE9D4/0x004FE304 in the opposite order to 0x004FC808's 0x004FE0A4/0x004FE88C pair; both functions test the same +0x1051 initialised byte.

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieTrack_UpdateAll
summary: The per-frame pump of the movie player: takes the player lock, feeds every due frame from the completion ring into the decoder (0x00518820/0x00518278/0x0051A210), advances the per-track timestamps and gives finished frames back. This is the function that turns queued buffers into decoded video/audio.
evidence: Drains the 0x40-entry ring at 0x007C805C, consumes 0x18-byte frame descriptors whose type byte +0x11 is 3, accumulates 64-bit sample/byte counters at +0x60, and calls the decoder API 0x00518010/0x0051A544/0x00518820/0x00518278/0x0051A210/0x0051867C; the only caller is the player's vtable-2 wait loop 0x004FC794.

name: maybe_Gfx_Movie_ShutdownTracks
summary: Tears the whole movie player down: stops every track, releases the deferred stopping event, frees each slot's handle and frame table, then frees the slot array itself and marks the manager closed. Called from the renderer reset path.
evidence: Called from maybe_Gfx_ResetRenderer (0x001B78F4) together with 0x004FE6F4; it calls 0x0051A4AC(handle,1) for all slots, uses software_interrupt(0x24)/0x23 (svcWaitSynchronization/svcCloseHandle), calls 0x00118100 on wait failure and frees the array through allocator slot +4; the '0xFFFFFFFF' written at 0x007AE160+8 is the closed marker.

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieTrack_Destroy
summary: Frees one movie track: closes its decoder handle (0x00519BE4) and gives the frame table back to the player allocator. Out-of-range indices are ignored.
evidence: Same index guard as the other track helpers over 0x007AE154; it is the per-slot body of the shutdown loop in 0x004FCC28 (identical 0x00519BE4 + allocator-free sequence).

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieTrack_Start
summary: Starts a prepared movie track: records the track's own index/array in the slot, then configures and starts the decoder channel (priority/stream id, volume or plane pointers, 0x0051A1CC/0x0051A1EC/0x00519D24/0x00519F94/0x00518A1C) and un-pauses it.
evidence: The sequence of decoder calls is the mirror of the pause/resume helpers (0x0051A4AC last with 0); slot fields +0x68/+0x6C are filled with 'track*7' and the slot array pointer, which only this function does; no callers, so it is invoked through a table or a script binding.

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieTrack_ResetQueue
summary: Drops all pending work for one track: stops its decoder channel, removes its entries from the 64-entry completion ring by pointer comparison, and zeroes the frame counters and timestamps.
evidence: It scans the same 0x007C805C ring as 0x004FC8A8 but nulls every entry that points at the slot, then clears +0x44/+0x48/+0x4C/+0x50/+0x58..+0x64; called from nowhere in the readable tree (table/vtable dispatch).

name: maybe_Gfx_Movie_WaitSurfacesIdle

params.self: surface set (4 ring slots at +0x18, 0x14 bytes each)

summary: Blocks until all four decoded-frame surfaces are free: it keeps pulling from 0x004FD4F4 and, when the ring is non-empty, counts how many slots are still in state 1 and waits on the surface event. Returns 1 when everything is idle and 0 when nothing was pending.
evidence: The ring mask is '&3' (4 surfaces) with 0x14-byte stride and state byte +0x18; the wait uses software_interrupt(0x24) (svcWaitSynchronization) plus 0x00118100 on error; callers 0x004FE6F4, 0x004FF3DC and 0x004FED58 are all movie teardown/flush paths.

name: maybe_Gfx_Movie_PresentFrame
summary: Presents one decoded frame: it asks the current ring slot how many lines are ready (source vtable +0x10), optionally halves the height for interlaced/field output, fetches the plane pointers (+0x18) and hands the Y/U/V rectangles to the Y2R conversion command 0x00501300, then advances the ring. Returns 1 when a frame was presented.
evidence: The callee 0x00501300 programs the Y2R service opened at 0x005012BC ('y2r:u' string at 0x005012F4): width/height plus three plane addresses with half-size chroma, exactly a YUV420 frame; the '&3' ring index and state byte +0x18 match 0x004FD3DC; SLOT 0x006B8D34 is consulted for the odd 'field' case.

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieSurface_Ctor
signature: u32 maybe_Gfx_MovieSurface_Ctor(GfxMovieSurfaces* self, u32 w, u32 h, u32 a, u32 b, u32 c)
summary: Constructor of the decoded-frame surface set (vtable 0x00780C3C, slot 0): allocates the two/three plane groups (3 channels x 2 buffers, 0x318 and 0x108 bytes each), converts the size words to floats for the decoder and wires the per-channel release helpers. Called once when a movie starts.
evidence: Occupies slot 0 of vtable 0x00780C3C = [0x004FD794, maybe_Gfx_StreamSlot_ReleaseSurfaces, 0x004FDE1C, 0x004FDE04]; it calls 0x004FE3F8/0x004FDAB4/0x00500F18 and VectorUnsignedToFloat on the plane sizes; the only caller is the movie setup at 0x001B7340.

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieBuffer_Ctor
signature: u32 maybe_Gfx_MovieBuffer_Ctor(GfxMovieBuffer* self, u32 fmt, u32 info, int frames, u32 streamId)
summary: Constructor of the decoded-frame buffer (vtable 0x00780C5C, slot 0): sizes the PCM/frame buffer as 8*stride*channels*frames*2 bytes, allocates it with the 32-byte alignment used by the DMA engine, and creates the matching track with 0x004FC230. Returns 1 on success.
evidence: Slot 0 of vtable 0x00780C5C = [0x004FDEE8, maybe_Gfx_StreamSlot_Destroy, 0x004FDFA4]; the size formula '*(info+8) * info->f_c * frames * 2' and the 0x20 alignment are what the later mixer/consumer 0x004FE6F4 expects; caller 0x001B7340 (movie setup) passes 1 and 0x10.

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieBuffer_Read
signature: bool maybe_Gfx_MovieBuffer_Read(GfxMovieBuffer* self, void* dst, u32 size)
summary: Copies finished frames out of the ring into a caller buffer and registers the copy with the completion queue (0x004FC694), keeping the ring's read/write positions in sync. Returns true when 'size' bytes were available and copied.
evidence: Slot 2 of vtable 0x00780C5C; it converts the ring's tick count to bytes via 0x004FCBB0/0x00300E18, then memcpy 0x00116A14 + 0x004FC694(track, dst, size) and advances the 64-bit counters at +0x18/+0x1C; '+0x14' is the wrap size and '+0x20' the partial count.

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieBuffer_Consume
signature: u32 maybe_Gfx_MovieBuffer_Consume(GfxMovieBuffer* self, u32 unused2, u32 unused3, int arg4)

params.self: buffer/decoder object with a mutex at +0x20
params.arg4: initial value handed to the state machine

summary: Feeds the decoder as many frames as it can take: it waits for the buffer thread state to settle (0x7/0x8), computes how many frames fit from the current free space, and calls the consume entry of each of the two streams that many times. Returns 1 when the object is in a usable state.
evidence: Calls 0x004FD4E4/0x004FD3DC/0x004FFD00 plus maybe_Os_MutexLock(0x00111D50) and sleeps 500,000 ticks between polls; the two stream slots at +0x484 are consumed through vtable '+0x1C' exactly like 0x004FF3DC; called from 0x001B78F4 and 0x004FE174 (movie frame pump).

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieThread_Stop

params.self: thread object at +0xAB0 of the movie context

summary: Moves the decoder thread object from 'running' (3) to 'stopping' (6), recording a tick stamp computed from the argument, and takes the object mutex. Returns 1 when the state allowed it and 0 otherwise.
evidence: State machine on self->f_c (3/6) shared with 0x004FE94C/0x004FE9D4; the timestamp arithmetic uses the 64-bit magic pair 0x20C49BA5E353F7CF (divide by 1000) at 0x004FE940..0x004FE948 and svc 0x28 (svcGetSystemTick); called from 0x004FC808, 0x004FE174 and 0x001B70E8.

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieThread_Start
summary: Moves the decoder thread object to state 5 ('starting') and waits, with 500,000-tick sleeps, until the worker reports state 3 ('running'). Returns 1 when the worker came up and 0 if it reported an error or shutdown.
evidence: Same state machine and 0x0007A120 (500,000) sleep constant as 0x004FE6F4; it uses maybe_Os_MutexLock on self+0x20 and the 0x0011CC94 sleep wrapper; called from 0x004FE174 and the movie setup 0x001B7340 right after creating the buffer.

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieThread_Join
summary: Stops the decoder worker (6 -> 5) and once it reports idle (3) adds the elapsed ticks to the two 64-bit counters at +0x150 and +0x158. Returns 1 when the worker stopped cleanly.
evidence: Mostly the same 64-bit tick arithmetic as 0x004FE88C but accumulating deltas into four words (+0x150..+0x15C) and comparing against the stored stamp at +0x168; the state sequence 6->5->3 matches 0x004FE94C/0x004FE88C; caller 0x004FC85C releases the reference that 0x004FC808 took.

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieDecoder_FeedVideo
summary: Pulls finished video samples from the demuxer ring and pushes them through the frame decoder into the surface that was just allocated: for every available sample it asks for the address/length (0x006B99B8), feeds the decoder vtable (+0x10/+0x14) and then hands the decoded surface to the output sink (+8). Active only while the selected video stream is not stopped.
evidence: Uses 0x006B9920/0x006B9948/0x006B99B8/0x006B9BB4, the VPU/VRAM block API already named Gfx_Vram_*/Gfx_GpuCmd_* by another batch, and the sink vtable at self+0x1D8 slot +8; the stream-select index at +0x560 and the ring mask '% 0x10' (16 entries) are shared with 0x004FEEF4.

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieDecoder_FeedAudio
summary: Second half of the demux pump: for each of the two audio/aux streams it takes finished samples, stores their timestamps in the per-stream 16-entry ring at +0x2A0/+0x4C0, forwards the payload to the stream decoder (+0x14) and releases the sample. Also flips the object into 'playing' when no data is left.
evidence: Two stream slots at +0x484/+0x488 with cmd 0x464/0x540, 16-entry stamp rings ('% 0x10') of 8 bytes, and the same 0x006B98B4/0x006B9948/0x006B99B8/0x006B9BB4 block API as 0x004FED80; state transitions use the shared 0..8 codes (4 = end of stream).

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieDecoder_CheckEndOfStream
summary: Checks whether the movie reached its end: it asks the demuxer for the stream status and, for codes 0x11/0x10/0x03, either marks the object finished (state 8) or failed (state 7) depending on whether frames are still buffered.
evidence: Calls 0x006B9BF4 (stream status) and compares against the literal codes 3/0x10/0x11 which are the demuxer's 'eof/error' values; it sets f_c = 7/8 and the flags 0x568 which 0x00500134 then interprets; caller 0x00500134 is the movie update entry.

name: maybe_Gfx_Movie_FlushStreams
signature: void maybe_Gfx_Movie_FlushStreams(GfxMovieContext* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int arg4)
summary: Flushes the two active stream slots of the movie player: drops every consumed frame from the surface ring, rewinds the read positions (0x48C/0x494) and stops the surface set. Called when a stream is released or re-selected.
evidence: Same body shape as 0x004FE6F4 (0x004FD4E4 + 0x004FD3DC + 0x004FFD00 then a 2-iteration loop over +0x484), but without the thread state machine; called only from Gfx_StreamSlot_Release (0x00500564).

name: maybe_Gfx_Movie_ReadTrackInfo
summary: Reads the movie's track table from the demuxer and sorts each track into the video (up to 8), audio (8) and text (8) arrays, storing the track ids and flags; on overflow it fails the object with the matching 0x568 flag bit. Also sets the 'tracks valid' byte at +0x11.
evidence: Uses 0x006B9920 (track count) and 0x006B9A8C(i,&info) where info word 0 selects the three arrays at +0x304 (0x28-byte video desc), +0x4A0 (0x10-byte audio desc) and +0x2A0 (8-byte text desc); the 0x568 bits 1/4/0x10 and 2/8/0x20 are set on overflow exactly as 0x001B7340 expects.

name: maybe_Gfx_Movie_ReadTextSamples
summary: Loads the subtitle/text samples: for every text track it fetches a sample, checks the 0x10-byte header (track id, size) against the video tracks, allocates a buffer with the context allocator and copies the payload; sets 'ready' (state 1) when done.
evidence: Text tracks live at +0x2E0 (8 max) and each sample is copied through func_00116A14 after a 0x10 header subtract; the same 0x006B99B8/0x006B9BB4 sample API as the video/audio feeders and the same 0x568 failure bits 0x80/0x100/0x200/0x400.

name: maybe_Gfx_Movie_SelectAudioTrack
summary: Switches the audible audio track: it waits until no frame is being handed over, detaches the previous track from the audio device (vtable +0xC), attaches the new one (+8) and returns 1 on success. -1 mutes the movie.
evidence: Uses the audio track array at +0x4A0 and the device object at +0x1D0/+0x1D8 (slots +8/+0xC take the context, the channel and the track descriptor); the 500,000-tick wait on the in-flight byte +0x564 matches 0x004FED80's handshake; called from 0x001B7340.

name: maybe_Gfx_Movie_SelectVideoTrack
signature: u32 maybe_Gfx_Movie_SelectVideoTrack(GfxMovieContext* self, int slot, int track)

params.slot: which of the two video surfaces (0/1)

summary: Binds a video track to one of the two decode surfaces: detaches the previous track (vtable +4) and attaches the new track descriptor (vtable +0), keeping the index table at +0x304 in sync. Returns 1 on success, 0 for an out-of-range track.
evidence: Video track indices are compared against the count at +0x300 and the per-slot index lives at +0x484/+0x488; the vtable at +0x1D0 slot 0 takes (context, channel, video descriptor) and slot +4 releases it; called twice from 0x001B7340 (slot 0 and 1).

name: maybe_Gfx_Movie_AdvanceTimeline
summary: Advances the playback timeline: it drains the surface ring through 0x004FD498/0x004FD2F4, moves both stream read cursors forward by one or two frames depending on the track's interlace flag and stores the timestamp of the next frame to present (+0x158/+0x15C). Waits 500,000 ticks while the needed frame is not decoded yet.
evidence: It is the only place that writes +0x158/+0x15C from the 8-byte stamp rings at +0x48/+0x4C, and it uses the '+0x32C < 2 ? 2 : 1' interlace rule also seen in 0x004FE6F4; called from 0x004FE6F4, 0x004FF3DC and 0x004FE174.

name: maybe_Gfx_Movie_Update
signature: void maybe_Gfx_Movie_Update(GfxMovieContext* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int arg4)
summary: Main movie state machine, called once per frame: drives the 0..8 states (open -> prepare tracks -> play -> end), reads track info, feeds the demuxer and drops already-shown frames. This is where a movie is actually advanced.
evidence: It is the only caller of 0x004FF4D4/0x004FF73C/0x004FED80/0x004FEEF4/0x004FF278 and dispatches on self->f_c (values 0,1,2,5,6,7,8), using the 0x568 flag word and the 0x1C byte as 'tracks valid'; called from 0x004FD264 (movie object tick).

name: maybe_Gfx_Movie_ReadThread

params.self: reader thread state (double buffer at self[2], handle pair at +0x68)

summary: Worker thread that streams the movie file: it waits on the two synchronisation handles, and whenever the 0x80000-byte double buffer has a free 0x40000 half it reads the next chunk through the file object's read slot (+0x24) and updates the 64-bit file position. Exits when the stop handle is signalled.
evidence: It waits with 0x005098E8 on two handles (self+0x68), guards the ring with the recursive lock at self+0x54, checks '0x80000 - (write - read)' and reads at most 0x40000 bytes through vtable +0x24, and calls 0x0011C814 on short reads; called from 0x001D6CEC.

name: Gfx_Y2r_Init
summary: Opens the 3DS 'y2r:u' colour-conversion service (YUV -> RGB) and stores the session handle at 0x007AE17C; also initialises the conversion registers. Called once before the first movie frame is converted.
evidence: The literal at 0x005012F4 is the service name string 'y2r:u' (verified at 0x0072D6F4 in the image) and it is passed to 0x001192C0 (srvGetServiceHandle) after 0x0011CCA0 (strlen); the handle lands in the global at 0x007AE17C which 0x00501300 then uses.

name: Gfx_Y2r_Convert
signature: void Gfx_Y2r_Convert(u32 srcY, u32 srcU, u32 srcV, u32 format, u32 a, u32 dstRgb, u32 dstRgb2, u32 dstRgb3, short w, short h, short stride, u32 fmtFlags, short outStride)
summary: Programs the Y2R unit for one frame - input Y/U/V plane addresses and sizes (U/V at half resolution), input format, output RGBA format, block/stride - and starts the conversion. This is the step that turns the decoded YUV movie frame into the RGB texture the renderer samples.
evidence: Every callee 0x0051A734/0x0051A750/0x0051A808/0x0051A8C0/0x0051A9B4/0x0051AB4C/0x0051AB84 writes a Y2R register block and the driver asserts on error via 0x00118100; the chroma planes are sized (w/2)*(h/2) while luma is w*h; only caller is the movie frame presenter 0x004FD4F4.

name: Gfx_Y2r_IsDone
summary: Polls the Y2R unit's busy flag and returns 1 when the conversion has finished (it inverts the driver's 'still busy' result). Used by the frame presenter before reusing the output surface.
evidence: One call to 0x0051ABAC plus '^ 1'; 0x0051ABAC reads the Y2R status register used by 0x00501300's driver, and the only caller is the presenter 0x004FD4F4 which must not overwrite a surface still being converted.

name: Svc_AcClient_OpenSession
summary: Reference-counted opener of the 'ac:u' service session: if the session is not open it allocates the service handle with 0x001192C0, bumps the reference counter and publishes the state. Returns 0 on success or the srv error code.
evidence: The literal at 0x00501660 is the service name 'ac:u' (verified at 0x0072FB84); it is combined with 0x0011CCA0 (strlen) and 0x001192C0 (srvGetServiceHandle), guarded by the recursive lock at 0x007E7900 and counted at 0x007AE908; caller-less in the readable tree because it is reached through 0x005016D8.

name: maybe_Svc_AcClient_CheckSession
summary: Cheap availability probe used by the UI: returns 0 when the 'ac:u' session is neither open nor usable, otherwise issues the small query 0x005019F4 and returns its first result byte.
evidence: Reads the same counter at 0x007AE908 as 0x00501554/0x00501774 and forwards the caller's r3 through 0x005019F4, which fills the IPC header 0x003E0042; called from 0x001CFFCC and maybe_Os_CriticalSectionTeardown (0x00501CFC).

name: maybe_Svc_AcClient_GetAccountState
summary: Returns the cached account state; when the value changed it refreshes it first (0x00501890) so the caller always sees a current answer.
evidence: Compares the result of command 0x00501B34 (IPC header 0x00050002) against the sentinel 0xE1209C46 and calls the close/reopen helper 0x00501890 on mismatch; called from 0x001CFFCC.

name: Svc_AcClient_IsSessionOpen
summary: Takes the client lock and reports whether the 'ac:u' session handle at 0x007AF094 is non-zero.
evidence: Three-instruction predicate over the global 0x007AF094 that 0x00501554 fills with the srv session; used as the fast path in 0x00501554 and 0x0050166C.

name: maybe_Svc_AcClient_Query
signature: int maybe_Svc_AcClient_Query(u32 cmd, u32* out, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Generic command dispatcher for the 'ac:u' client: it sends the command via 0x00501B70, lazily opens the session (0x0010C694 + 0x0050F200) when needed, then forwards to one of the command senders (0x00501C8C/0x00501A98/0x00501A40). Returns the command result.

name: Svc_AcClient_CloseSession
summary: Closes the 'ac:u' session if it is open, dropping the service handle (0x0050F244) and clearing the open flag. Safe to call repeatedly.
evidence: Mirror of 0x00501554: tests the open byte at 0x007AE904, calls 0x0050F244 (handle release) and 0x0050F2C4 (refcount decrement), all under 0x007E7900; called by 0x0050171C, 0x00501D14 and the critical-section teardown.

name: Svc_AcClient_Cmd003E0042
